Both queries scope positively to %/lib/ansible/% (the shipped package), which leaves the top-level test/, hacking/, examples/, docs/, contrib/, changelogs/ and bin/ trees out of the candidate tables without extra exclusion logic. The direct filesystem-operation sink families (open, os/shutil/tarfile/zipfile/glob/shelve/tempfile, archive extraction, makedirs_safe/unfrackpath wrappers) include %/lib/ansible/modules/% because modules execute on managed nodes and their file operations are real sinks fed by task arguments; the source families and the os.path propagation/validation family are restricted to the controller tree (lib/ansible minus modules) because the captured input boundaries (task args, task_vars, lookup terms, CLI, remote result parse) are controller-side, and module-side propagation rows would be source-free noise.

scoring.result: No web framework matched (all scores 0.0 < 0.50); references/fastapi.md, flask.md and django.md were NOT loaded. Ansible is a CLI/agentless automation engine: the role a web framework plays elsewhere is played here by ansible's own plugin architecture (ansible.plugins.loader loading action/lookup/callback/connection/filter plugins, the CLI dispatcher in lib/ansible/cli, and the Task/DataLoader/Templar pipeline in executor/parsing/vars). No reference file exists for that architecture, so the source/sink shapes were derived from repository evidence plus references/python.md and references/patterns.md only, as WORKFLOW.md 4.2.3 prescribes for the no-framework case. Assumptions are recorded in this file.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: ansible has no HTTP surface, so the untrusted-input boundaries are: (1) playbook/task arguments after templating (playbook YAML, --extra-vars, and remote ansible_facts all merge into self._task.args), (2) task_vars host variables (inventory + remote facts, incl. task_vars['inventory_hostname'] used as a fetch dest path component), (3) lookup plugin terms, (4) the operator CLI (sys.argv, CLI.__init__ args, context.CLIARGS: --roles-path, -i, --vault-password-file, --tree), (5) os.environ/os.getenv (ANSIBLE_CONFIG etc., operator trust level), (6) remote module output parsed by json.loads (_parse_returned_data), (7) result['ansible_facts'] merged into host variables, (8) tar member names of galaxy-downloaded role archives. The sink side funnels through builtin open(), os/shutil/tarfile/zipfile APIs, the os.path pipeline, and three ansible-internal wrapper chains (DataLoader, ActionBase/ActionModule, connection put_file/fetch_file).

guardsAndEvidence.evidence: galaxy/role.py:323-:329 - only member.isreg()/issym() are extracted; parts are built from member.name.replace(archive_parent_dir, '', 1).split(os.sep) and a part is dropped when part == '..' or '~' in part or '$' in part; the surviving parts are re-joined with os.path.join and extracted into self.path. Absolute-path members: os.path.join(*final_parts) with a leading '/' component yields an absolute path only if the first surviving part is absolute (leading '/' parts become '' after split, so re-joining yields a relative path); however isreg() symlinks (issym) extract link targets verbatim - the target string is not filtered.

plugins/action/fetch.py:118-:123 - when dest ends with os.sep, base = os.path.basename(source_local) is joined onto dest (basename neutralizes directory traversal in the filename); :123 `if not dest.startswith("/")` sends relative dests through self._loader.path_dwim (search-path resolution, dataloader.py:173-:186); the non-flat branch at :128-:132 does NOT basename source_local - the full remote path (which can be remote-returned via slurpres.get('source') at :100-:102) is appended under <dest>/<inventory_hostname>/.

utils/path.py:65-:87 - rpath = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(path)) is computed and existence checked before os.makedirs (EEXIST race tolerated, other OSErrors raised); guards directory creation only, not the file write that follows (fetch.py:168 then open(dest, 'wb') at :175 - TOCTOU between the realpath check and the open remains).

parsing/dataloader.py:181 (path_dwim), :222 (path_dwim_relative), :283 (path_dwim_relative_stack) - `if given.startswith(to_text(os.path.sep)) or given.startswith(u'~')` treats the value as absolute/homedir and returns it (expanded via unfrackpath) instead of joining the basedir; relative values are joined onto the basedir - this is resolution, not containment: there is no base-directory containment check (no realpath-relative_to style guard) anywhere in the DataLoader.

utils/path.py:31-:62 - os.path.expanduser + os.path.expandvars + optional os.path.realpath + os.path.normpath, joined onto a basedir when relative (expandvars means environment variables inside paths are substituted).

plugins/action/copy.py:117-:125 - os.path.islink followed by os.path.realpath and os.path.isfile on the target; local_follow controls whether symlinked files are dereferenced (symlink targets outside the source tree are copied when local_follow=True).

extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries (10 columns) for codeql query run + bqrs decode; @kind problem is intentionally NOT set (wrong shape for candidate tables - it requires exactly element+string) and @kind table is not assumed to exist
extraction.matchKindSemantics: api = call resolved to the real stdlib API through API graphs (API::moduleImport(moduleHint).getMember(member).getACall(), alias-aware); ast = syntax-level shape match (module-qualified attribute calls, name calls, attribute/subscript reads, parameter definition rows). The same call site may legitimately appear as both an api and an ast row (identical to the airflow project of this series); labeling dedupes by file/line/signature. All source families and all wrapper/definition families are ast rows by construction; only the os/shutil/io/tarfile/zipfile/glob/shelve sink family has api rows.
exclusions: %/ansible-db/% (CodeQL database nested in the source tree) - excluded from every row in both queries

positive scope %/lib/ansible/% in both queries: top-level test/, hacking/, examples/, docs/, contrib/, changelogs/ and bin/ trees are never candidates (bin/ansible* wrappers contain no filesystem operations; they only pass sys.argv into lib/ansible/cli, which is captured by the cli_args family)

sources.ql and the os.path/propagation+wrapper families in sinks.ql exclude %/lib/ansible/modules/%; the direct filesystem-operation families in sinks.ql include modules (documented in database.locationNote)

uncoveredCases: module.params boundary (remote-side mirror of self._task.args): ~28k read sites across 3908 modules - deliberately NOT extracted (would drown the candidate table); modules are covered on the sink side only. A future module-focused pass should add module.params[...] / module.params.get(...) families with module_spec argument filtering.

%-format path construction: plugins/action/fetch.py:132 dest = "%s/%s/%s" % (self._loader.path_dwim(dest), target_name, source_local) and :134 dest.replace("//", "/") - the BinaryExpr modulo operator cannot be told apart from numeric modulo without type resolution, so no BinOp family is emitted; the taint step must be added later in MySummaries.qll if the pass-1 flow needs it. Same for string concatenation with + and f-strings (none observed constructing paths in the audited controller tree).

remote result dict reads beyond the json.loads boundary: values extracted from parsed module results, e.g. fetch.py:100-:102 remote_source = slurpres.get('source') (the remote-returned expanded path that REPLACES the fetch source and flows into source_local -> dest construction) and copy.py:355-:356 dest = dest_status_nofollow['lnk_source'] - not captured as source rows (dynamic result dicts); the boundary is captured one step earlier at the _parse_returned_data json.loads row (family remote_result).

self._task.args.pop(key) / .copy() / iteration forms: the bare self._task.args attribute row (family task_args) covers the receiver node, but the pop/copy call nodes themselves are not separate rows; set_fact.py:42 args.pop('cacheable') and task_executor.py:573-:581 _variable_params splicing are the concrete sites.

shell-plugin remote path joining and quoting: plugins/action/fetch.py:71 self._connection._shell.join_path(source) and :106 _unquote - remote-side semantics implemented per shell plugin (plugins/shell/*.py), out of the controller path-traversal scope; only _remote_expand_user (ActionBase) is captured as an action_file_api wrapper.

dynamic plugin loading: ansible.plugins.loader resolves action/lookup/callback plugin paths from configuration (collections paths, DEFAULT_ACTION_PLUGIN_PATH etc. via config/manager + unfrackpath); plugin file names are operator-configured, not attacker-controlled, and the loader's os.path.join/exists chains are captured by the generic os.path families only where they occur in the controller tree.

os.fdopen is not a sink family: its argument 0 is a file descriptor from tempfile.mkstemp (copy.py:389, assemble.py:44, action/__init__.py:442, dataloader.py:326) - the tempfile family rows record the mkstemp calls with the dir= keyword destination (argIndex -1).

`from os import path` alias form matched only in the three files that use it (plugins/action/include_vars.py, module_utils/infinibox.py, module_utils/pure.py); other aliased os.path imports (`from os.path import basename/expanduser` at playbook/role_include.py:21, module_utils/azure_rm_common.py:14, plugins/callback/*.py) would need from-import name matching - the basename/expanduser call sites there are low-value for pass 1 and are left to labeling via the generic families if they use qualified forms.

receiver-name collisions: the .extract/.extractall/.extractfile family is receiver-agnostic (possible non-archive receivers survive to labeling); the os.path name-form family is restricted to the three `from os import path` files; task_vars/variables/result/member/path name matches are ordinary local names but restricted by family shape and (for variables/result/member) by file path conditions.
API-graph/syntax double rows: the same os.* call site can yield one api row and one ast row (matchKind differs) - intentional, identical to the airflow project; labels.json deduplication handles it.
async/await handlers: not applicable (no async file handlers in the controller tree; ansible uses threads/processes, and the connection plugins' put/fetch implementations are synchronous).
